citation: 'Louis Wahl.' Wood engraving of the Louis Wahl residence, 964 (now 2026) Prairie Avenue, Chicago, from the oblique front, in 'The Homes of Chicago', The Land Owner (Chicago: J. M. Wing), May 1874; unknown engraver. Reproduced on chicagology.com, Prairie Avenue, 2026 S. Prairie.
author: unknown engraver for The Land Owner (J. M. Wing, publisher)
repository: chicagology.com (secondary reproduction of the plate). Prairie library image a20-chicagology-2026-wahl-landowner-1874 (chicago/prairie_1904_v1/research/images/stream-2000-2100.json), its file in the image store (STORE.json); the same file is committed at data/sources/assets/wahl_2026_landowner_t3608/wahl_2026_landowner_1874.jpg.
locator: The whole vignette: the house from the walk south-east of it, its street front from the south corner to the tower at its north end, a parkway tree hiding the front between them; the south flank back to its canted bay; the stoop under the balcony; the low rear wing with a veranda and a summer house on the lawn south of the house; the fence along the walk. The camera solve (data/reference_views/house_2026_prairie/landowner_1874.json) locates every feature read off it.
rights_note: A US periodical illustration published in 1874, in the public domain; the web reproduction is a faithful copy of a two-dimensional work and adds no right of its own. Read for forms, counts and proportions; no texture or other asset is derived from it.
access_notes: Read 2026-11-16 (T-3608) from the image store's copy, 1400 x 1125 px, sha256 f09857bdce3dcfe247a804f71d873471ae1ecf2699c66a2be5a02092d09dcd48 (the store's display copy of the library's fetch of 2026-10-02 from chicagology, 1447 x 1163 px). chicagology.com is not reachable from the build containers, so this copy is the one read.
note: The only located picture of 2026 Prairie. From the walk south-east of it, it shows a Second Empire house of two tall storeys over a raised stone basement under a slated mansard: every window round-headed under an arched hood; a bracketed cornice over a deep frieze; at the street front's north end a pavilion standing forward of the front, two round-headed lights a storey in its face, carried up under a mansard of its own with iron cresting over a pierced frieze; immediately south of it the door at the head of a straight stoop under a balcony on consoles, a pair of narrow lights over it; the south flank in shadow (the engraver's convention for the turned face) with one light a storey, a tall stack rising from its cornice up the mansard, and a canted bay further back carried up into a mansard of its own with a dormer; beyond the bay a lower rear wing with a veranda, and on the lawn south of the house an octagonal summer house; a low fence on the street line. The street front between the corner and the door is hidden behind a parkway tree. The camera is solved from the 1911 sheet's plan points, so each height read off it is a measurement through that solve.
